title: Bidirectional A* in Reykjavik: meet in the middle!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* race from start and goal across real street connectivity in Reykjavík’s Vesturbær. The two frontiers meet early, reducing explored nodes while preserving optimal routes on a weighted road graph.
ig_caption:
🚦🏙️ Bidirectional A* in Reykjavík (Vesturbær) — can you feel the “meet-in-the-middle” speed?

In this visualization, we model the city as a **weighted graph**: intersections become nodes and road segments become edges (with costs like distance or travel time). **Bidirectional A*** runs two synchronized A* searches—one forward from the start and one backward from the goal—each guided by an admissible heuristic (e.g., straight-line distance) to prioritize promising routes. ✅

🧠 Why it’s powerful: instead of expanding outward from only one side, the algorithm **cuts the search space** dramatically, and when the forward and backward frontiers intersect, we stitch together the optimal path consistent with the graph’s edge weights.

📍Real street maps = real geometry + real constraints → great for understanding how graph search behaves under uneven layouts, varying segment weights, and heuristic-driven pruning.

👉 Want Part 2 for a different neighborhood (and a different heuristic)? Comment your favorite start/finish pair!
fb_caption:

📌 Graph theory takeaway: roads form a weighted graph, and A* uses a heuristic to intelligently expand nodes instead of brute-forcing every option. If you enjoyed this, share it with a friend learning algorithms—what city should I map next?
